verification_report.summary: The full supplied chapter is correct under the two hypotheses expressly allowed for the bounded lower-mass corollary. The geometry, positivity criterion, every heat-kernel estimate, completed-square identity, asymptotic bound, cutoff and gluing step were checked directly. Attribution agrees with Theorem 1.1 and the supplied proofs in [Xia–Zhang, A counterexample to the bounded mass property](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.21053). The theorem-search service returned unrelated results; the required web fallback located the primary source. No XZ26 lemma was accepted without checking its proof. With ddc=i partial bar-partial/(2pi), integral_P2 omega_FS^2=1 and beta restricts to 2dA_E, so integral_X omega^3=6. Stokes gives the excess mass as 3 integral_X dV wedge dcV wedge alpha^2; its vertical component yields exactly 6 times the fiber energy. Independently, the source coefficient 12pi becomes 6 after accounting for both cubic mass scaling and the squared base-form scaling. The Fourier eigenvalues are pi^2 p^2+q^2/4, with spectral gap 1/4. Gaussian unfolding, the variance formula and Parseval justify the heat equation, logarithmic Hessian bound, all differentiated large-time estimates and energy 2eta^2 log(1/t)+O(eta^2), with the claimed uniformity. The nearest-lattice argument proves the Gaussian gradient estimate, and the numerical constants in square absorption are sufficient, uniformly when kappa is replaced by kappa chi^2. Expanding the square reproduces every term of Q exactly. The initial transition contributes O(eta) pointwise defect; the stated small-time and large-time bounds integrate to o(1), while the negative slope is O(sqrt(eta log(1/eta))). Products of mixed derivatives also satisfy the large-time quotient estimate. On the cutoff interval, exp(-1/(5e eta))=o(exp(-x_*)), so the error is smaller than the remaining transverse positivity. Continuity and support of d_eta and the lower bound 2/27 on [-2,-1] follow as claimed. A smooth strict majorant with arbitrarily small integral excess exists; the ordered supports give -m_eta<=g_eta'<=0, and g_eta'' corrects Q without changing fiber energy. All three positivity tests hold globally, including both extension regions. On the fixed base ball, energy equals 2log(1/eta)+O(eta^2), proving smooth mass divergence. The main construction uses neither bounded approximation nor Bedford–Taylor continuity, and assumes no BMP, Kahler condition or PVP. Using the two stipulated hypotheses only in the lower-mass corollary gives v_-=6 and v_+=infinity. The final internal general-theory specialization r_3=1 and polynomial damping q>1 agrees with the available improved-range chapter context. No novelty, optimality or universal nonexistence conclusion is inferred. No critical errors or gaps were found.
